Hi Elena / Tom — great talking earlier. Quick answers and an action plan below.

Recommended models (short):
- redwood-embed-2 (512d): good balance of recall and index size; tuned for short product blurbs.
- openembed-lite (256d): lower storage/latency; may lose fine-grained recall on synonyms.
- redwood-embed-2-quant (int8): when index cost is a concern; expect slight drop (~1-2% normalized MRR).

Evaluation metrics we'll produce by EOD Monday:
- Recall@10, Recall@100 (business-critical for discovery)
- MRR (mean reciprocal rank) for prioritized queries
- Cosine similarity distributions (match vs non-match)
- Index size & avg query latency (95th pct)
- Drift signal: mean pairwise distance change and PCA explained variance shifts between baseline and new data

Risk register (summary):
- Quality regression: risk if model variant (quantized / 256d) loses niche-synonym recall. Mitigation: keep fallback to redwood-embed-2 and run prompt-set-specific evals.
- Dimensionality mismatch: 256d vs 512d affects nearest-neighbor density — mitigation: re-rank with cross-encoder on top 50 results for sensitive flows.
- Index churn / cold cache latency: mitigation: warm indexes and precompute heavy queries during onboarding window.
- Drift detection false-positives: tune threshold on simulated historical windows first.

Proposed mutual action plan:
1) We run a 5-day embedding fit (sandbox) with your 2k sample + up to 50 prioritized queries — deliverables are the metric report + recommended model.
2) If results look good, expand to 50k docs and provide index sizing & cost projections.
3) Optional: we deliver a small re-ranker recipe (cross-encoder prompt set) for product detail pages.

We'll attach a short risk register and the exact eval commands. Ben and Neha are cc'd to coordinate scope and commercial terms if you want to proceed after NDA.

Action items (from us): attach: prompt-sets-v1.tsv, a short evaluation checklist, and embed-risk-register.xlsx.

Best,
Jasmine
